questions.question: How do you configure a User Task in Flowable Design to allow multiple specific users to claim it?
questions.optionA: Assign it to an expression resolving to a single user
questions.optionB: Add users to the "Candidate users" property
questions.optionC: Set the task to "Parallel Multi-instance"
questions.optionD: Use a Script Task to assign it

questions.question: When configuring an Exclusive Gateway, what is the best practice to handle a situation where no conditional sequence flows evaluate to true?
questions.optionA: Use an Event-based Gateway instead
questions.optionB: Configure a "Default flow" property
questions.optionC: Let the process throw an unhandled exception
questions.optionD: Add a Timer Boundary Event

questions.question: What is the primary difference between a Sub-process and a Call Activity in Flowable?
questions.optionA: A Sub-process is reusable across different Apps; a Call Activity is not.
questions.optionB: A Sub-process is embedded in the same diagram; a Call Activity calls an external, reusable process.
questions.optionC: They are identical in execution and design.
questions.optionD: Call Activities cannot contain User Tasks.

questions.question: In a Multi-instance User Task configured sequentially, what happens when the first user completes their task?
questions.optionA: The entire process moves to the next node.
questions.optionB: The task is terminated.
questions.optionC: A new task is generated for the next item in the collection.
questions.optionD: All remaining users get parallel tasks.

questions.question: What is the function of a Compensation Boundary Event in a BPMN process?
questions.optionA: To pause the process until an employee is paid.
questions.optionB: To undo or compensate for a previously completed activity when an error or cancellation occurs.
questions.optionC: To automatically allocate budget to a financial system.
questions.optionD: To retry a failed Service Task infinitely.

questions.question: How do you map a variable from a parent process to a child process invoked by a Call Activity?
questions.optionA: Variables map automatically by default.
questions.optionB: Configure the "In parameters" mapping on the Call Activity.
questions.optionC: Use a Message Event to send data.
questions.optionD: Use a Script Task to update the database directly.

questions.question: How do you configure a Timer Event using ISO 8601 syntax to trigger repeatedly, such as every 3 days?
questions.optionA: Using the syntax `R/P3D`
questions.optionB: Using the syntax `REPEAT: 3 DAYS`
questions.optionC: Repeating timers are not supported in BPMN
questions.optionD: Using a `cron` expression like `* * 3 * *`

questions.question: What happens if a Non-interrupting Timer Boundary Event triggers on a User Task?
questions.optionA: The User Task is cancelled, and the process follows the timer flow.
questions.optionB: The User Task remains active, and a parallel path is spawned from the timer flow.
questions.optionC: An error is thrown.
questions.optionD: The process pauses completely.

questions.question: In Flowable, what is required to trigger a specific Message Catch Event from an external system?
questions.optionA: Only the process instance ID.
questions.optionB: The Message Reference name and optionally a correlation key.
questions.optionC: The Task ID of the next User Task.
questions.optionD: An Error Code.

questions.question: Which attribute must match for an Error End Event to be caught by an Error Boundary Event?
questions.optionA: The name of the events
questions.optionB: The Error Code
questions.optionC: The user assigned to the task
questions.optionD: The process version

questions.question: How can you prevent an asynchronous Service Task from blocking the main process thread in Flowable?
questions.optionA: Mark it as "Exclusive" = False
questions.optionB: Set "Asynchronous" to True on the Service Task properties
questions.optionC: Put it in a separate Sub-process
questions.optionD: Change it to a Script Task

questions.question: How are UI forms bound to a Start Event so users can input data when initiating a process?
questions.optionA: By writing custom HTML script inside the Start Event properties.
questions.optionB: By selecting a created form model in the "Start form reference" property.
questions.optionC: Start Events cannot have forms attached to them.
questions.optionD: By attaching a User Task immediately before the Start Event.

questions.question: In an Inclusive Gateway split, what happens at the corresponding converging Inclusive Gateway?
questions.optionA: It waits for only the first token to arrive.
questions.optionB: It waits for all tokens that were generated by the split to arrive before continuing.
questions.optionC: It throws an error if more than one token arrives.
questions.optionD: It merges tokens without waiting.

questions.question: In Flowable, what is the default history level setting for the process engine that dictates how much audit data is saved?
questions.optionA: None
questions.optionB: Activity
questions.optionC: Audit
questions.optionD: Full

questions.question: What is the effect of checking the "Is executable" property on a Process model?
questions.optionA: It allows the process to be deployed and instantiated in the runtime engine.
questions.optionB: It converts the process to executable Java code.
questions.optionC: It locks the model from further editing.
questions.optionD: It bypasses all User Tasks during testing.

questions.question: What does a small diagonal "slash" (/) across a sequence flow line exiting an Exclusive or Inclusive Gateway indicate?
questions.optionA: A broken connection that needs fixing.
questions.optionB: The default sequence flow to take if no other conditions are met.
questions.optionC: An asynchronous continuation boundary.
questions.optionD: A mandatory parallel path.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about an Event Sub-process?
questions.optionA: It must be triggered by an external REST call.
questions.optionB: It can only be triggered by a Message Event.
questions.optionC: It is embedded within a process and triggered by an event (like Error or Timer) within that scope.
questions.optionD: It replaces standard Call Activities.

questions.question: How do you configure a Service Task to call a specific Java class delegated to handle the logic?
questions.optionA: Select "Java class" and provide the fully qualified class name in the "Class" property.
questions.optionB: Select "Expression" and write Java code inline.
questions.optionC: Use a Script Task instead.
questions.optionD: Configure a REST endpoint URL.

questions.question: In a Business Rule Task, how is the task typically linked to a DMN Decision Table in Flowable Design?
questions.optionA: By writing JUEL logic
questions.optionB: By referencing the Decision Table's Model Key in the "Decision table reference" property
questions.optionC: By embedding the DMN XML
questions.optionD: By using a Call Activity

questions.question: What is a "Signal Event" in BPMN used for compared to a "Message Event"?
questions.optionA: Signals are point-to-point (one-to-one), Messages are broadcast.
questions.optionB: Signals are broadcast to all active handlers, Messages are point-to-point to a specific handler.
questions.optionC: Signals are only for errors, Messages are for timers.
questions.optionD: There is no functional difference in Flowable.

questions.question: When a User Task is assigned to a "Candidate group", how does a specific user begin working on it?
questions.optionA: It is automatically assigned based on alphabetical order.
questions.optionB: The user must first "Claim" the task.
questions.optionC: The engine runs a round-robin assignment.
questions.optionD: Any group member can complete it without claiming.

questions.question: What does the "Completion condition" property do on a Multi-instance activity?
questions.optionA: It defines when the multi-instance execution should end early (e.g., when 50% are approved).
questions.optionB: It validates the form data before completion.
questions.optionC: It checks if the database is online.
questions.optionD: It sends an email when all tasks are done.

questions.question: How do you define a constant, default value for a process variable directly within the BPMN diagram?
questions.optionA: Use an Initialization Task.
questions.optionB: Define a Data Object or map it in the Start Event form.
questions.optionC: You can only do this via REST API.
questions.optionD: Use a Boundary Event.

questions.question: What is fundamentally required at the engine level to successfully execute a Mail Task in Flowable?
questions.optionA: A connected SMTP server configured in the Flowable engine properties.
questions.optionB: A custom Java delegate class deployed with the App.
questions.optionC: An active email client installed on the user's local machine.
questions.optionD: A REST API endpoint hosted on a third-party server.

questions.question: How can you map specific process variables to be explicitly passed out of a child process (Call Activity) back to the parent process?
questions.optionA: Variables are never passed back; they are destroyed when the child ends.
questions.optionB: Using the "Out parameters" mapping in the Call Activity properties.
questions.optionC: By using a database trigger to sync the tables.
questions.optionD: By catching a Message Event in the parent process.
